layout.reset.what: put the view on screen back to the arrangement it is declared with, which is the way back from a layout somebody has docked into an unusable shape
layout.reset.answers: The view on screen only: the other views keep whatever was done to them. Popped-out windows are not pulled back in. Refuses when no interface is attached.

panel.close.what: take a panel out of the layout, giving the room to what is left

params.name: name
params.what: the panel to close; an unknown or missing name is refused with the list of the ones there are

panel.close.answers: Whether the panel was open is not asked, only whether it exists: closing one that is not in the layout answers the same way and does nothing, which is what the caller wanted anyway. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: clear the rail before a screenshot

panel.dock.what: bring a popped-out panel back into the main window, which is the other half of panel.pop_out and the only way back for a window a compositor has hidden

params.name: name
params.what: the panel to dock; an unknown or missing name is refused with the list of the ones there are

panel.dock.answers: `where` is always "layout". A panel that was never popped out is docked where it belongs rather than refused. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: put the map back in the main window

panel.open.what: put a panel in the layout, switching to the view it belongs to on the way, which is how the panels no view starts with are reached at all

params.name: name
params.what: the panel, spelled as panels.list spells it; an unknown or missing name is refused with the list of the ones there are

panel.open.answers: It answers once the panel has been asked for, not once it is drawn: the layout is the frame loop's, and the change lands on the next frame. A panel already in the layout is left where it is. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: bring up the waterfall from a script

panel.pop_out.what: send a panel out into a window of its own, so a second monitor can hold what the layout has no room for

params.name: name
params.what: the panel to pop out; an unknown or missing name is refused with the list of the ones there are

panel.pop_out.answers: `where` is always "window", the verb having only one destination: it is there so an answer read on its own says what happened. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: give the map a monitor to itself

window.close.what: close a panel's own window, which returns the panel to the main layout rather than losing it

params.name: name
params.what: the panel whose window is closed; a panel that is not in a window of its own is refused

window.close.answers: Refuses when no interface is attached, and refuses where the interface has no window manager behind it.

example.what: close the window a capture no longer needs

window.open.what: open a panel in a window of its own, the same act as panel.pop_out under the name a caller thinking in windows reaches for

params.name: name
params.what: the panel to give a window; an unknown or missing name is refused with the list of the ones there are

window.open.answers: The window is asked for here and opened by the frame loop, so the answer says it was accepted rather than that a window is up. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: watch the waterfall beside the map
